newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambian court says no polls until complaints heard.
newsitem.headline: Zambian court says no polls until complaints heard.

text.p: Zambia's high court ruled on Friday that all elections should be postponed until petitions, filed by the opposition after controversial general elections last year, were heard.

Opposition parties led by former president Kenneth Kaunda's United National Independence Party (UNIP) won their request for an injunction restraining Zambia' Electoral Commission from organising local polls until their petitions were dealt with.
"The Supreme (high) Court has ruled that there will be no elections until the opposition complaints have been given a hearing and a ruling made," a court official told Reuters.

Local government elections, which were scheduled to be held in 1995, were deferred for lack of logistics and were expected to be held early this year. The Electoral Commission was also preparing to hold a parliamentary by-election next week.

The opposition is challenging the legitimacy of the November 18 elections in which the ruling Movement for Multi-party Democracy (MMD) won a landslide victory. They said that the voters register was incomplete and fraught with errors.

Opposition parties have also filed petitions challenging President Frederick Chiluba's credentials as a candidate. They claim the president lied in claiming to have been born in Zambia when he filed his electoral nomination papers.
Hearings on the petitions continue next week.
